inputs.share_count_basis: Shares in issue 511.054m less 1,850,000 shares repurchased in June 2026 and cancelled 16-Jul-2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note 18(c)) = 509.204m. Interim note 8(b): no dilutive potential ordinary shares. Shares held by the share-award trust (weighted average 505.8m implies ~3-5m) are deliberately NOT deducted because they exist to be granted to employees. Held FLAT: the share-award purchases are charged as SBC in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: No equity-settled share-based payment EXPENSE recognised FY2022-H1 FY2026 (H1 FY2026 interim: 'did not incur equity settled share-based expenses'; last expense US$21.1m in FY2021 pre-IPO). The company instead buys shares on market for its share award scheme: US$2.557m FY2024, US$4.049m FY2025, US$9.080m H1 FY2026 (statement of changes in equity, note 18(b)). Those purchases are the cash cost of future employee awards and are charged as SBC here (FY2025 US$4.049m = 0.25% of revenue; projected at 0.3% of revenue). Equity-award taxes nil (no net-share settlement).
inputs.fx_note: USD flows -> HKD quote at USD/HKD 7.8479 (Yahoo USDHKD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-17T21:00Z). HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band, so the rate is a near-constant; no dual listing for a parity check. Cross-check: interim repurchase HKD29,428,891 = USD3,757,000 implies 7.833 in June 2026, consistent.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.1 x 5.0% ERP + ~0.5pp for a HK-listed, PRC/Vietnam-manufacturing mid-cap = cost of equity ~10.3%; debt is ~11% of capital at ~3.5% pre-tax. WACC 9.5%, identical across scenarios. Tariff, customer-concentration and cyclicality risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities US$19.5m (8.056 current + 11.440 non-current, 30-Jun-2026) are in total_debt / net_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from flows; D&A includes right-of-use depreciation and capex_pct carries ~0.4pp of revenue for lease-asset renewal.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (FY2025 NCI profit US$0.09m, NCI equity US$0.2m); flows treated as fully attributable, no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Chervon is an operating manufacturer of cordless OPE (EGO) and power tools (FLEX/SKIL/DEVON) - routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). Net debt at 30-Jun-2026: bank loans 252.822 + lease liabilities 19.496 - cash 372.208 - structured deposits/wealth-management products 34.504 (current FVPL, cash-like) = -134.394 (net cash). Pledged deposits US$20.75m excluded: they secure letters of credit and bills payable and are working capital. Non-current FVPL insurance product US$6.9m added in the equity bridge. Interest income (US$6.47m FY2025) is stripped from the FCF anchor because the cash that earns it is in the bridge; the engine flows are EBITDA-based and unlevered so it is not in them either. Working capital: trade receivables + inventory - trade payables was ~42% of revenue at Dec-2025 (459+448-223 = 684 vs 1,628), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture -25% of the revenue change. FY2025 reported FCF (155.8) was flattered by a working-capital release as revenue fell 8.2%; FY2023 FCF -262 was the destocking trough - neither is a mid-cycle base, hence the component build. Buybacks: HK$150m programme announced Aug-2026, US$3.76m spent in H1 FY2026 (financing outflow); the company IS a (small) repurchaser, and share-award purchases fund the flat count. SBC-near-zero market: house and street differ only by the ~0.3% of revenue share-award charge, so the band is narrow.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 29.1% is inflated by the Dec-2021 HKEX IPO raise (equity 284 -> 797 in FY2021) and diverges >30% from revenue (6.3%) and EPS (11.6%); equity 3yr CAGR 2.5% is depressed by the FY2025 special dividend (US$118.7m paid). Neither is a usable organic growth signal, so revenue 5yr CAGR is selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - share-award purchases/SBC - interest income): FY2020 80.5, FY2021 76.0, FY2022 -53.1, FY2023 -269.9, FY2024 84.4, FY2025 145.3. 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (FY2022 base negative). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (12.5%) exceeds reported (8.8%) only because FY2020 carried a US$21.1m pre-IPO SBC charge; it is end-point-driven by the FY2025 inventory release and should not be read as trend.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: H1 revenue +12.8% to 1,029.1 plus H2 ~+8% on H2 FY2025's tariff-depressed 715.4 = ~1,800 (+10.5%). Then mid-single-digit growth in line with the 5yr revenue CAGR (6.3%), decaying to 3% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin history 12.4% FY21, 11.3% FY22, 0.7% FY23 (destock), 11.9% FY24, 10.8% FY25. FY2026 12.5% reflects H1's record 39.3% gross margin incl. one-off tariff refunds; FY2027 eases to 12.0% as refunds do not recur, then 12.5% mature on OBM/EGO mix. D&A 3.3% (FY2025 ~55/1,628). Capex 4.9% while Vietnam capacity is built out (FY21-25 range 3.6-6.4%, FY2025 4.5%) easing to 4.3% incl. lease renewals. Cash tax 17% (FY24/FY25 effective rate 15.1%; PRC HNTE 15%, US 21%, cash taxes paid ran above the P&L charge in FY2025).

scenario_narratives.base: H1 FY2026's recovery holds but H2 normalises: FY2026 revenue ~US$1.8bn (+10.5%) and EBITDA margin 12.5% flattered by tariff refunds, easing to 12.0% in FY2027 before EGO/OBM mix lifts it back to a 12.5% mid-cycle level - roughly the FY2021/FY2024 peaks, not above them. Vietnam capacity absorbs the US book by end-2026, so tariffs become a cost of doing business rather than a recurring shock. Growth settles at the 5yr revenue CAGR (~6%) on EGO category expansion, the John Deere battery tie-up and European distribution, fading to 3%. Working capital (~42% of revenue) consumes a quarter of each incremental revenue dollar, which keeps owner-FCF margins near 5-6%.
scenario_narratives.bull: EGO compounds as the North American cordless-OPE category leader: robotic mowers (Europe 2026), commercial riding mowers via John Deere dealers, and new categories add a growth leg while FLEX/SKIL finally reach scale through new Walmart/Tractor Supply/Canadian Tire distribution. OBM rises above 80% of sales and EBITDA margin climbs to 15% - TTI-like - as Vietnam's cost base matures. Revenue grows 13% in FY2026 and high-single-digits for four years.
scenario_narratives.bear: H1 FY2026 was a restocking pull-forward by a handful of big-box customers (top 5 = 58% of revenue, top 1 = 35%): H2 FY2026 weakens and FY2027 revenue falls 4% as inventories reverse, repeating the FY2023 pattern in milder form. Tariff policy re-escalates or US Customs targets Vietnam-origin goods, the tariff refunds that lifted H1 margins prove one-off, FLEX/SKIL keep losing money against TTI and Stanley Black & Decker, and DEVON is capped by the China property slump. EBITDA margin settles at 10% (FY2025 was 10.8%) and growth runs at 2-3%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: a single customer is ~35% of revenue, US-China tariff policy was the dominant swing factor in FY2025 and remains unresolved, and H1 FY2026 growth was partly restocking with a precedent (FY2023 revenue -31%) for sharp reversal. Base 50%: H1 FY2026 delivered and Vietnam capacity is on track. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent wins at once (robotic mowers, Deere channel, FLEX/SKIL scale, margins above any prior peak).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Chervon is valued as a cyclical consumer-durables manufacturer on mid-cycle margins, not on H1 FY2026's record. The stock has more than doubled off its 52-week low on that half; the model asks what a mid-cycle 12-12.5% EBITDA margin, a working-capital-heavy growth model and a 13x terminal cap are worth, with risk carried once in the scenario weights.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer concentration: largest customer ~35%, top five ~58% of FY2025 revenue
US-China tariff policy and potential Vietnam country-of-origin/transshipment scrutiny
Restocking pull-forward in H1 FY2026 reversing (FY2023 destock precedent: revenue -31%, FCF -US$262m)
Working capital intensity (~42% of revenue) means growth converts poorly to cash
One-off tariff refunds inside H1 FY2026's record 39.3% gross margin
RMB appreciation against the USD reporting currency (US$13.9m FX loss in H1 FY2026)
